subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Reactivity 2.2 How fast? The rate of chemical change
Reactivity 2.3 How far? The extent of chemical change

questions.q: According to collision theory, a reaction occurs when particles collide with:
questions.explain: Only collisions with energy at least equal to the activation energy and the right geometry lead to reaction.

questions.q: The minimum energy needed for a successful collision is the:
questions.explain: Activation energy (Ea) is the energy barrier that must be overcome for reaction.

questions.q: Increasing the temperature increases reaction rate mainly because:
options: More particles have energy above the activation energy and collisions are more frequent
questions.explain: Higher temperature raises particle energy and collision frequency, increasing the proportion of successful collisions.

questions.q: A catalyst increases the rate of reaction by:
options: Providing an alternative pathway with lower activation energy
Being used up in the reaction
questions.explain: Catalysts lower Ea and are not consumed overall.

questions.q: Increasing the surface area of a solid reactant increases rate because:
options: More particles are exposed for collisions
questions.explain: Greater surface area allows more frequent collisions at the solid's surface.

questions.q: Increasing the concentration of a reactant in solution generally:
options: Increases the rate by making collisions more frequent
questions.explain: More particles per unit volume means more frequent successful collisions.

questions.q: On a Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution, raising the temperature:
options: Shifts the curve to higher energy, increasing the fraction above Ea
Has no effect on energy spread
questions.explain: A greater proportion of molecules then exceed the activation energy.

questions.q: A dynamic equilibrium is reached when:
options: The forward and reverse reaction rates are equal
questions.explain: At equilibrium concentrations stay constant while both reactions continue at equal rates.

questions.q: Le Chatelier's principle predicts that a system at equilibrium responds to a change by:
options: Shifting to oppose (partly counteract) the change
questions.explain: The equilibrium position moves to reduce the effect of an imposed change.

questions.q: For an exothermic forward reaction, increasing the temperature shifts the equilibrium:
questions.explain: Raising temperature favours the endothermic (reverse) direction, reducing product yield.

questions.q: Increasing pressure on the equilibrium N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3 shifts it:
options: Towards the side with fewer gas moles (products)
questions.explain: There are 4 gas moles left and 2 right, so higher pressure favours the product side.

questions.q: Removing a product from an equilibrium mixture will:
options: Shift the equilibrium towards the products (more product forms)
questions.explain: The system responds to replace the removed product.

questions.q: A catalyst affects the equilibrium position by:
options: Not changing it, but reaching equilibrium faster
questions.explain: A catalyst speeds up forward and reverse rates equally, so it changes rate, not position.

questions.q: A large value of the equilibrium constant Kc indicates that at equilibrium:
questions.explain: A large Kc means the equilibrium lies well to the product side.

questions.q: The equilibrium constant expression for aA + bB ⇌ cC + dD is:
questions.explain: Kc is products over reactants, each raised to its stoichiometric coefficient.

questions.q: Which change would NOT increase the rate of a reaction between a solid and an acid?
questions.explain: Lowering temperature decreases rate; the others increase it.

questions.q: At equilibrium, the concentrations of reactants and products are:
questions.explain: Constant concentrations, set by Kc, are maintained though forward and reverse reactions continue.

questions.q: A catalyst is described as not being consumed because it:
options: Is regenerated by the end of the reaction
questions.explain: It participates in the mechanism but is reformed, so the overall amount is unchanged.

questions.q: For the endothermic reaction of forming products, increasing temperature will:
questions.explain: Higher temperature favours the endothermic (forward) direction, increasing product yield.

questions.q: Doubling the concentration of both reactants in a simple bimolecular reaction would be expected to increase the collision frequency and hence the initial rate. This best illustrates that rate depends on:
questions.explain: Higher concentrations increase collision frequency and reaction rate.
